producer_report.summary: Every throughput review run now compares the latest median minutes per landed job and the per-stage medians with the previous review's, even while a design request is open. It names the stages whose median grew, largest first, in the record's note, in the `athena drain` line and in a UI line. When the median grew by more than 25% (SLOWDOWN_RATIO, strict), code queues a Priority: high request without asking the model. Its title is `Throughput slowdown: <stage> grew from <prev> to <now> min per landed job`, and the body gives the median change and all grown stages. It cites no review id, so throughput_followups cannot read it as the change implementing a design proposal. An open request with the `Throughput slowdown: ` marker stops a duplicate. The previous per-stage medians are rebuilt from job records with no schema change. status.rs gains `StageMinutes::median_of`, shared with `Throughput::compute`, and `landed_jobs_among_first`, which cuts over all landed jobs so unmeasured ones do not shift the window. hestia.rs gains is_slowdown, stage_growth, previous_stage_medians, slowdown_request, open_request_with_marker, review_subject, throughput_outcome and `compare_with_previous_review`. The commit subject and the drain line now show a queued slowdown request. Docs: hestia.rs module comment, hestia.md section 12 and a CHANGELOG entry. records.rs has doc-comment changes only. New tests cover the 25 to 60 rise with an open design request (and a second review), unmeasured jobs before the earlier review, a flat median, the 24.5 and 25.1 band against 20, the pure helpers, the request text, the subject and the outcome line.

open_issues: Open question from the plan, unresolved: per-stage medians are not stored in athena.throughput-review/1. The previous window is a reconstruction (a landing record written after a review can move a job's rank). Storing them would need a schema change.
The 25% decision uses the recorded previous median. If the median grew over 25% but no stage median grew, or the previous window cannot be rebuilt, nothing is queued and the note says so.

mistakes: A first draft of test A asserted known.throughput_reviews == vec![review]. The fixture's earlier review is also in the records, so I changed it to a contains check before the first run.
learnings: throughput_review stores landings as Throughput::landed_total, which counts every landed request job. landed_jobs drops landed jobs with no invocation, so cutting landed_jobs by that count drifts. landed_jobs_among_first fixes this by ranking over all landed jobs first.

timed_job with StageMinutes::default() yields a landed job with only a request and an outcome. It counts in landed_total and not in landed_jobs. Truncating its records to the request gives an open request job.
StewardRequest::new rejects a body with lines that look like acceptance bullets; the slowdown body keeps its stage list on one line.

Each comparison is against the previous review, so a persistent slowdown is flagged again only if the median again rose by more than 25% over the prior review. An open slowdown request stops a duplicate meanwhile.
